Subject: Stellara — order intake checklist & line-item mapping

Hi Jared / Stellara procurement team,

Thanks for agreeing to kick off onboarding with Redwood. To get purchase order (PO) issuance and invoicing working smoothly, can you confirm the following items and return the attached vendor intake form? We want to avoid back-and-forth on line items and remittance details once we start issuing POs.

Quick checklist (please reply inline):
- Legal company name and billing remit-to address (as it should appear on Redwood POs)
- Tax ID / VAT registration (attach W-9 or equivalent)
- Preferred invoice email and AP contact (we prefer a dedicated procurement address)
- Supported currency(s) and whether you accept consolidated monthly invoices or require per-PO invoices
- Required PO fields: vendor code, department/project code, Redwood GL code, unit description length limits (we supply a sample template)
- Line-item rules: do you need quantity/unit-price breakdowns, SKU codes, or one consolidated line per invoice?
- Early payment discounts or special payment terms (we default to Net 30)
- Banking details for ACH/wire (remit-to), and whether Redwood should include both billing and shipping addresses on the PO

Attached: stellara_vendor_intake_form.pdf and order-lineitem-template.csv (sample CSV showing how we encode line items and GL mapping).

Target timeline: if we get answers + completed intake form by EOD Friday (Jun 4), we can issue a test PO the following week and enable production POs within ~10 business days, assuming no tax or banking hold-ups. If you need a faster turnaround, call me and we can prioritize.

Action items:
- Jared / procurement: return intake form + any vendor documents (W-9, bank letter)
- Laura (Finance): confirm any Redwood-specific GL fields or vendor codes we must provide on the PO
- Marcus / Vivek (Ops): I'll need you to review the CSV mapping once the vendor returns it

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.

Best,
